definitions.title: Probability conventions
definitions.latex: Put $I=[0,1]$. We identify a copula with its probability law $\mu_C$ on $I^2$. Write $\lambda$ for Lebesgue probability measure on $I$, $\pi_1(u,v)=u$ and $\pi_2(u,v)=v$ for the coordinate projections, and $f_*\mu(A)=\mu(f^{-1}(A))$ for the pushforward of a measure. All displayed integrals use Lebesgue measure.
definitions.bridge: Foundation: probability measures, pushforwards, Lebesgue measure

definitions.title: Bivariate copula
definitions.latex:
A probability law $\mu_C$ on $I^2$ is a bivariate copula precisely when
\[\left(\href{#def-probability}{(\pi_1)_*\mu_{C}} = \href{#def-probability}{\lambda} \;\land\; \href{#def-probability}{(\pi_2)_*\mu_{C}} = \href{#def-probability}{\lambda}\right).\]

definitions.title: Distribution function
definitions.latex:
For $u,v\in I$, the distribution function associated with $\mu_C$ is
\[C(u,v):=\href{#def-probability}{\mu_{C}([0,u]\times[0,v])}.\]

definitions.title: Real powers and derivatives
definitions.latex: Real powers have their usual nonnegative-base meaning in this proof. $f'(r)=d$ asserts that the derivative exists and equals $d$. Strict increase on $[a,b]$ means $f(x)<f(y)$ whenever $a\le x<y\le b$; strict decrease reverses that inequality.
definitions.bridge: Foundation: Real.rpow, HasDerivAt, StrictMonoOn, StrictAntiOn, min

The upper boundary (equation 4)
definitions.latex: For $r\in[-1,1]$,\[\Phi(r)-r=\begin{cases}g_-(r),&-1\le r\le0,\\g_+(r),&0\le r\le1.\end{cases}\] The two branches agree at zero. These are the two expressions used in the original proof.

definitions.title: Supported on a graph
definitions.latex: The statement that a copula is supported on the graph of $f$ means $v=f(u)$ for $\mu_C$-almost every $(u,v)$, equivalently $\mu_C(\{(u,v):v=f(u)\})=1$. Both maps here are continuous.

definitions.title: The extremal copula
definitions.latex: $D_{1/2}$ is the law of $(U,T(U))$ for $U$ uniform on $[0,1]$. The checked law identity identifies it with the paper's $D_c$ at $c=1/2$.

definitions.title: The survival copula (equation 8)
definitions.latex: The survival copula of $C$ is the law of $(1-U,1-V)$ when $(U,V)$ has law $C$. Its distribution function is\[\widehat C(u,v)=\left(\left(u + v\right) - 1\right) + C(\href{#def-probability}{(1-u)},\href{#def-probability}{(1-v)}).\]

changes: The whole statement and proof of Corollary 3.2 are retained in the comparison column, from the published version of 23 September 2026.
The two scalar branch expressions are named g₋ and g₊. Derivative existence, strict monotonicity, and every equality case are explicit.
Attainment and uniqueness are expressed as equivalences; the extremizers’ coefficient values and support graphs are included.
Copulas are identified with their probability laws. Supported on a graph is interpreted as probability one on that graph; the graphs here are closed.
Theorem 1.1, Lemma 3.1 and the survival identities remain compiled dependencies, as they are cited dependencies in the printed proof.

original.latex:
\begin{corollary}[Sharp deviation between $\nu$ and $\rho$]
\label{cor:nu-rho}
Every $C\in\CC$ satisfies $|\nu(C)-\rho(C)|\le\frac14$.
The maximum $\nu-\rho=\frac14$ is attained only by $D_{1/2}$, which has $\rho=0$ and is supported on the graph of the tent map $u\mapsto\min\{2u,2-2u\}$.
The minimum $\nu-\rho=-\frac14$ is attained only by its survival copula, which is supported on the graph of $u\mapsto|2u-1|$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
On $[-1,0]$, \eqref{eq:Phi-def} gives $\Phi(r)-r=r+1-\frac34(1+r)^{4/3}$, and its derivative $1-(1+r)^{1/3}$ is positive for $r<0$.
On $[0,1]$, $\Phi(r)-r=1-r-\frac34(1-r)^{4/3}$, and its derivative $(1-r)^{1/3}-1$ is negative for $r>0$.
Consequently $\Phi(r)-r\le\Phi(0)=\frac14$, with equality only at $r=0$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:rho-nu-values} matches $r=0$ with $c=\frac12$, so by Theorem~\ref{thm:rho-nu}, no copula other than $D_{1/2}$ attains the maximum.
Its coupling $\gamma_{\zeta_{1/2}}$ sits on the graph of $\zeta_{1/2}(x)=|2x-1|$ from \eqref{eq:Zc-def}, which becomes the graph of the tent map in the coordinates $(u,v)=(1-x,1-z)$.
For the minimum, \eqref{eq:survival-transform} sends $\nu-\rho$ to $\rho-\nu$, so only $\widehat{D_{1/2}}$ attains it: this is the copula of $(X,\zeta_{1/2}(X))$, supported on the graph of $u\mapsto|2u-1|$.
\end{proof}
